papers.title: Remote monitoring of symptoms using a smart device in Parkinson's disease: a randomized pilot trial.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Effective, timely management of Parkinson's disease (PD) symptoms is crucial for improving patient outcomes. This study evaluated the effectiveness of remote monitoring of symptoms using smart wearable devices in patients with PD over a 6-month period. METHODS: This open-label, randomized study (SHARE-PD) included patients with PD who were assigned to the smart device group (received medical care from physicians based on symptoms and activities data collected using MONIPAD) or the regular medical care group. The primary endpoint was the Movement Disorder Society Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (MDS-UPDRS) total score. Secondary endpoints included quality of life (QoL), patient satisfaction, and impact of MONIPAD data on treatment decisions. RESULTS: In total, 110 patients were enrolled, with 52 and 54 patients included in the smart device group and the regular medical care group, respectively. The smart device group showed significant improvements in the MDS-UPDRS total score compared with the regular medical care group (between-group difference: -11.1 points, 95% confidence interval: -15.2, -7.1; p < 0.0001). Improvements were also observed in aspects of QoL and patient satisfaction versus the regular medical care group. The time to first prescription change was substantially shorter in the smart device group (55.7 [32.1] days vs 92.9 [50.7] days). CONCLUSIONS: Remote monitoring of symptoms using smart wearable devices significantly improved clinical outcomes, QoL, and patient satisfaction in patients with PD. These improvements may be attributed to enhanced shared decision-making, facilitated by timely and effective communication between patients and physicians, leading to more personalized and proactive disease management.

papers.title: Reply to correspondence: Gastrointestinal determinants of levodopa response in Parkinson's disease: An integrated perspective.
papers.abstract: levodopa pharmacokinetic variability in Parkinson's disease, and we agree that gastrointestinal determinants of treatment response extend beyond gastric emptying. However, our review was deliberately focused on gastroparesis, while explicitly acknowledging that levodopa is absorbed in the duodenum and proximal jejunum and that gastrointestinal dysfunction in Parkinson's disease may involve more generalized transit abnormalities, small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, and gut microbiota-related mechanisms. Importantly, prolonged small bowel transit alone does not establish the direction or magnitude of its effect on levodopa bioavailability, nor does current evidence demonstrate that intestinal dysmotility is a more direct or predominant determinant than delayed gastric emptying. Rather than opposing gastric and intestinal mechanisms, we propose that gastric emptying, small bowel motility, and other pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and disease-related factors should be viewed as sequential, interdependent, and patient-specific determinants of levodopa response. Integrated studies combining gastrointestinal transit assessment, levodopa pharmacokinetics, and motor outcomes are therefore warranted.

papers.title: Timing of rehabilitation therapy initiation and all-cause mortality in parkinson's disease: nationwide cohort study.
papers.abstract: Rehabilitation is integral to Parkinson's disease management yet remains underutilised, with limited evidence on long-term survival impact. Using Korean National Health Insurance Service data, we identified 19,153 individuals newly diagnosed with Parkinson's disease (2006-2023) who received rehabilitative developmental therapy. Stratified by rehabilitation initiation timing and disability severity at initiation, Cox proportional hazards regression estimated adjusted hazard ratios [HR]s for all-cause mortality. Compared with rehabilitation within 1 year of diagnosis, delays of 1-2 years and ≥2 years were associated with 28% (HR 1.28, 95% CI 1.21-1.35) and 44% (HR 1.44, 95% CI 1.37-1.51) higher mortality hazard, respectively. Mortality hazard increased progressively with disability severity (21% for mild-to-moderate, 45% for severe). Earlier rehabilitation consistently reduced mortality across all disability subgroups with a dose-response trend, with no statistically significant interaction between timing and disability severity (P = 0.503). These findings support systematic rehabilitation referral at Parkinson's disease diagnosis.

papers.title: Computer vision-derived gait-state tracking of acute treatment response in Parkinson's disease: external and prospective validation.
papers.abstract: Continuous, treatment-responsive measurement of motor state is an unmet need in Parkinson's disease and a broad challenge for digital biomarkers: clinical gait scales are coarse and ordinal, and most digital measures are never validated beyond their derivation setting. We present a digital biomarker derived from full-mesh 3D human-pose reconstruction in standard monocular video, built from high-contrast within-patient treatment transitions and applied to out-of-sample patients. In a retrospective cohort (53 patients) it discriminated treatment states (cross-validated AUROC 0.88) and defined a continuous motor-state axis. Across six independent cohorts (266 subjects, 3,591 walks, eight sites, three continents) it showed consistent medication effects in the two medication-labelled cohorts and tracked clinical gait impairment in the four cohorts carrying clinical gait ratings; in a prospective cohort (21 patients) it preserved ordered transitions for medication and deep brain stimulation. On identical paired observations it was more responsive than the ordinal MDS-UPDRS Part III item 3.10 (standardized response mean 1.29 versus 0.83 internally, 0.92 versus 0.54 externally); its finer resolution also registered directional within-patient improvement more often, an advantage of measurement resolution that reaches parity once change is required to exceed the minimal detectable change, supporting a scalable, generalizable measurement tool. This graphic explains a computer-vision method for tracking acute treatment response in Parkinson's disease using standard monocular video without specialized hardware. It shows three steps: first, a single camera records the same patient before and after therapy; second, a markerless full-mesh 3D pose is reconstructed frame-by-frame; third, a gait-state biomarker is derived, with Levodopa and deep brain stimulation moving patients up the biomarker axis from negative to positive values. papers.title: Synergistic interplay between triazine and curcumin or resveratrol in mitigating rotenone-induced toxicity in Drosophila model.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuronal loss, oxidative stress, and debilitating motor dysfunction. Targeting the Wnt signaling pathway provides a powerful disease-modifying strategy. Building on recent evidence that triazine derivatives modulate Wnt signaling, we used a Drosophila model and in silico molecular docking to validate the specific interactions driving this pathway modulation, followed by qPCR of key Wnt signaling-related genes: armadillo, wingless, and frizzled 3. The neuroprotective efficacy of the triazine derivative, alone or in combination with curcumin or resveratrol, was subsequently evaluated using behavioral, neurochemical, biochemical, apoptotic, immunohistochemical, and ultrastructural assessments. Treatment with the triazine derivative produced marked neuroprotective effects, which were further enhanced when combined with curcumin or resveratrol. This treatment significantly restored dopamine levels and locomotor performance, enhanced superoxide dismutase and catalase activities, and reduced lipid peroxidation compared with untreated rotenone-exposed flies. Moreover, immunohistochemical analysis indicated attenuation of apoptotic signaling, while transmission electron microscopy revealed substantial preservation of neural ultrastructure. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the neuroprotective potential of the triazine derivative and suggest that its combination with curcumin and resveratrol may provide an enhanced strategy for counteracting oxidative stress, neural apoptosis, and motor dysfunction associated with PD. The findings further support Wnt signaling modulation as a promising mechanistic target and provide a rationale for further investigations of triazine-based combination strategies as potential disease-modifying approaches for PD.

papers.title: Evaluation of Submandibular Gland Biopsies With Real-Time Quaking-Induced Conversion in Clinical Parkinson Disease.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The definite diagnosis of Parkinson disease (PD) is usually made by the detection of α-synuclein aggregates in the brain postmortem with the rare exception of some genetic forms. Traces of α-synuclein aggregates in extracerebral tissue biopsies may serve as an appropriate biomarker to confirm a clinical diagnosis in vivo. We set out to determine whether the detection of α-synuclein aggregates in submandibular gland biopsies is an effective means for diagnosing patients with PD. METHODS: In this prospective study, we consecutively acquired and examined submandibular gland biopsies from patients with clinical PD in neurologic care and controls who underwent surgical procedures on the submandibular gland for different reasons. Our index method was the detection of α-synuclein aggregates using the real-time quaking-induced conversion (RT-QuIC) in fresh-frozen tissue. We compared the results with immunohistochemical α-synuclein aggregate detection and paraffin-embedded tissue blot (PET-blot) as reference methods in formalin-fixed tissue from the same biopsy. RESULTS: The study population included 25 patients with clinical PD (mean age 67.3 ± 9.3 years, 64% male, 36% female) and 25 age-matched controls (mean age 64.6 ± 8.6 years, 48% male, 52% female). The RT-QuIC assay detected α-synuclein aggregates in submandibular gland biopsies (n = 41) with a sensitivity of 81.8%, which increased to 90% after a clinical follow-up, and a specificity of 100%, thus providing an accuracy of 90.2% (95% CI 76.6%-96.4%) and 95.1% (95% CI 82.9%-98.7%), respectively. The PET-blot with mAb5C12 (n = 49) confirmed 50% of the RT-QuIC positives and offered a sensitivity of 45.8% (50% after clinical follow-up) and a specificity of 100%. Cortical thinning and altered directed connectivity in Parkinson's disease: a cortical thickness-guided voxel-wise granger causality study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Parkinson's disease (PD) involves both regional cortical degeneration and large-scale network dysfunction. This study examined whether cortical regions showing structural abnormalities in PD also exhibit altered directed connectivity. METHODS: Sixty-two patients with PD and 46 healthy controls underwent structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). Whole-brain cortical thickness was analyzed using FreeSurfer. Regions showing significant cortical thinning were used as seeds for voxel-wise Granger causality analysis (GCA). Associations between imaging measures and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores were examined using partial correlation analyses. RESULTS: Patients with PD showed significantly reduced cortical thickness in the right medial superior frontal gyrus (SFGmed.R) and right precentral gyrus (PreCG.R), with no regions showing significantly greater cortical thickness than healthy controls. Compared with controls, patients with PD exhibited increased GCA from SFGmed.R to the left inferior temporal gyrus and from PreCG.R to the calcarine/medial visual cortex, whereas decreased GCA was observed from PreCG.R to the left supramarginal gyrus and from the right superior temporal gyrus and left olfactory-related region to PreCG.R. SFGmed.R cortical thickness was positively associated with MoCA scores after adjustment for age, sex, and education level, and this association remained significant after Bonferroni correction for seven exploratory correlation analyses (partial Spearman's ρ CONCLUSION: Cortical thinning in frontal-executive and motor regions of patients with PD is accompanied by altered directed interactions with distributed sensory and associative regions. Medial superior frontal cortical thickness may also be related to global cognitive performance.

papers.title: The protocol for a phase 2A, multi centre, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study to assess the effect of 12 weeks treatment with oral PXS-4728A on microglia activation, as measured by positron emission tomography, in participants with isolated rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Isolated REM-sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD) is a well-described prodromal feature of synuclein diseases, including Parkinson's disease (PD), dementia with Lewy bodies and, less frequently, multiple system atrophy. Neuroinflammation has been reported in iRBD and is potentially a major contributor to synuclein accumulation and propagation. Positron emission tomography (PET) imaging of the translocator protein (TSPO) overexpressed by activated microglia has been used to demonstrate neuroinflammation in both iRBD and manifest PD. Although immune-modulating therapies have not shown direct benefit in PD, there are to date no reported trials in prodromal disease. This paper describes the protocol for the first immune-modulating drug trial in iRBD, which could provide evidence for an early neuroprotective intervention strategy in prodromal PD. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This is a phase IIa, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial of the small molecule PXS-4728A in iRBD. Forty participants with definitive iRBD, one or more features of Parkinsonism, impaired olfaction and/or impaired colour vision will be randomised 3:1 (treatment: placebo) for a 12-week treatment period, followed by a 12-week washout. The primary outcome will assess the effect of PXS-4728A on neuroinflammation, measured by PET using the TSPO radioligand [11 STUDY PROTOCOL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05904717; Identifier, NCT05904717.

papers.title: Redefining drug-induced tremor: a mechanism-based framework for clinical and etiological assessment.
papers.abstract: Drug-induced tremor (DIT) encompasses clinically diverse syndromes with different mechanisms, clinical courses, and management needs. This Perspective proposes a mechanism-based approach to guide evaluation and management by integrating tremor phenotype, drug pharmacology, associated neurological findings, and clinical course. The initial assessment considers peripheral adrenergic amplification, dopamine receptor blockade or depletion, and systemic or neurotoxic effects, while allowing drug-specific assessment when mechanisms are less clearly understood, as with valproate and serotonergic antidepressants. These considerations guide treatment adjustment and targeted investigation. Associated cerebellar, neuropathic, cognitive, or systemic findings guide evaluation for neurotoxicity and metabolic abnormalities. When tremor is accompanied by parkinsonian features, clinical follow-up assesses recovery, persistence, or progression. Dopamine transporter (DAT) imaging is considered when uncertainty about coexisting nigrostriatal degeneration would affect management. Assessment also considers tardive tremor, taking into account its clinical features and the timing of symptoms in relation to prolonged drug exposure and withdrawal. By connecting these assessments to investigation, treatment, follow-up, and counseling, the proposed framework complements the Movement Disorder Society tremor classification and provides a practical approach to the heterogeneity of DIT. Prospective validation is needed to determine its clinical utility.

papers.title: Acute central metabolic effects of otolithic vestibular stimulation in a non-human primate model of Parkinsonism: proof-of-concept neuroimaging and functional study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Vestibular dysfunction has increasingly been recognized in the pathophysiology of Parkinson's disease (PD), particularly in relation to postural instability, gait impairment, and altered sensorimotor integration. However, the central metabolic effects associated with acute targeted otolithic vestibular stimulation remain poorly understood. OBJECTIVES: To explore the acute metabolic correlates associated with otolithic vestibular stimulation using 18 METHODS: A unilateral otolithic vestibular implant was placed in a macaque (Macaca fascicularis RESULTS: MPTP administration induced a persistent parkinsonian phenotype characterized by marked deterioration in fine motor performance relative to baseline, together with persistently elevated Kurlan motor scores throughout follow-up. Metabolically, the MPTP-induced condition was associated with relative hypermetabolism involving especially audiovestibular cortical areas, accompanied by relative hypometabolism in frontal executive, paralimbic, and visual associative regions. Acute vestibular stimulation (ON vs. OFF) demonstrated state-dependent metabolic differences across post-implantation evaluations. During stimulation, increased metabolism predominantly involved vestibulo-thalamo-striatal, sensorimotor, and limbic-paralimbic networks. In contrast, OFF conditions showed relatively greater involvement in visual associative cortices and cerebellar vermis. CONCLUSION: Acute otolithic vestibular stimulation was associated with metabolic modulation of vestibulo-thalamo-striatal and sensorimotor-related networks in a parkinsonian non-human primate model. These findings provide proof-of-concept evidence supporting the capacity of vestibular neurostimulation to engage distributed central motor integration circuits.

papers.title: Animal and Cell Models in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's Disease: Current Innovations Reviewed.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) remain major global health challenges due to their complex pathology and lack of curative therapies. Advancing therapeutic strategies requires reliable experimental models that recapitulate disease mechanisms. This review summarizes recent developments in animal and in vitro models for AD and PD, with emphasis on their translational relevance and applications. Transgenic mice (APP/PS1, 3xTg-AD), α-synuclein and LRRK2-based models for PD, rat 6- OHDA systems, zebrafish, and non-human primates provide valuable insights into amyloid deposition, tau aggregation, synaptic dysfunction, and motor impairment, though each presents limitations in faithfully mimicking human disease. Complementary in vitro approaches using neuronal and glial cell lines enable targeted studies on oxidative stress, inflammation, amyloid-beta (Aβ) toxicity, tau pathology, and dopaminergic degeneration. Emerging platforms such as CRISPR/Cas9-based editing, induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived organoids, and artificial intelligence-driven drug discovery are further expanding the preclinical landscape. Together, these integrated strategies enhance understanding of neurodegenerative processes and hold promise for the development of effective disease-modifying therapies.

papers.title: Relationship between age-related factors and Lewy body scores in Parkinson's disease.
papers.journal: The journal of medical investigation : JMI
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: In Japan, the number of patients with late-onset Parkinson's disease (PD) is increasing (1). These patients tend to exhibit a wider range of motor and non-motor symptoms as well as cognitive impairment compared to middle-aged onset cases (2, 3). OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to determine whether neuropathological changes consistent with the clinical characteristics of late-onset PD patients differ across brain regions. METHODS: A consecutive autopsy series of 38 patients, at Osaka Toneyama Medical Center (from the years 2005-2024), with clinically and pathologically confirmed sporadic PD, who were aged 50 years or older at the time of onset, were studied. The age of onset, sex, age at death, disease duration, Lewy body (LB) score and Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology were analyzed. RESULTS: The correlations between age at onset and limbic LB score, age at death and both the limbic and total LB scores were found to be significant, with Spearman's correlation coefficients of 0.363, 0.430 and 0.339, and p-values of 0.025, 0.007 and 0.037, respectively. CONCLUSION: The late-onset PD patients have more LBs, especially in the limbic system, than the younger-onset PD patients at the end stage of their clinical course. J. Med. Invest. 73 : 474-481, August, 2026.

papers.title: Prolonged developmental TiO₂ nanoparticle exposure at environmentally relevant level drives Parkinson's disease-related phenotypes in Caenorhabditis elegans.
papers.abstract: Titanium dioxide nanoparticles (TiO₂-NPs) are widely used in consumer and industrial products and are increasingly released into aquatic environments, raising concerns about their potential health risks. The nematode Caenorhabditis elegans has emerged as a valuable bioindicator of water pollution and a practical toxicological tool for water quality monitoring. Here, we investigated the effects of prolonged developmental TiO₂-NP exposure on the development of Parkinson's disease (PD)-related phenotypes in C. elegans and explored the underlying mechanisms. Two transgenic strains were used: BZ555, which expresses green fluorescent protein in dopaminergic neurons, and NL5901, which constitutively expresses human α-synuclein (α-syn) in muscle. Prolonged developmental exposure to 0.1 µg/mL TiO₂-NPs, a concentration comparable to the upper range of previously reported TiO₂ engineered-particle concentrations in surface waters, 1 and 10 µg/mL TiO₂-NPs increased α-synuclein-associated fluorescence in NL5901 worms, and induced dopaminergic neuronal abnormalities in BZ555 worms. TiO₂-NPs (1 and 10 µg/mL) also elevated a whole-worm oxidative signal in BZ555 worms. The dopaminergic neuronal abnormalities observed after 84 h developmental exposure and the impaired basal slowing behavior observed under a separate 24 h exposure paradigm (1 and 10 µg/mL) provide complementary evidence that TiO₂-NPs can disrupt dopaminergic function. Moreover, mechanistic analysis revealed that TiO₂-NPs at 1 µg/mL upregulated skn-1, gst-38, and gcs-1, key regulators of the antioxidant defense system, following TiO₂-NP exposure. papers.title: Diffusion-Model-Guided Identification of a Candidate α-Synuclein Aggregation Inhibitor under Secondary-Nucleation-Dominated Conditions.
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry letters
papers.abstract: The process of α-synuclein aggregation results in the formation of amyloid deposits that accumulate in the brain of patients affected by Parkinson's disease and related synucleinopathies. Among possible therapeutic strategies for these conditions, one approach is based on the development of compounds capable of inhibiting α-synuclein aggregation. An effective inhibition could be achieved by blocking the nucleation sites on the surface of the amyloid fibrils that are responsible for their autocatalytic proliferation. Here, we use an E(3)-equivariant conditional diffusion model to identify candidate inhibitors of this type. With this approach, we generated pocket-conditioned molecules, identified purchasable analogues, and experimentally tested selected compounds. We thus identified a compound that delays α-synuclein aggregation under conditions in which secondary nucleation is the dominant process. These results illustrate the use of conditional diffusion models to identify candidate aggregation inhibitors.

papers.title: Reconsidering early Parkinson's disease: dopaminergic hyperactivation as a pre-degenerative functional stage.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurological condition primarily caused by the death of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc). However, recent research suggests a functional hyperactivity phase that precedes neuronal degeneration and may hold therapeutic potential. This study was conducted as a narrative review to synthesize evidence on early-phase dopaminergic hyperactivation in PD and different interventions that could potentially delay the onset of PD. We identified various toxins and genetic mutations that increase neuronal excitability, which eventually progresses to depletion of SNc neurons. This disrupts the circuitry of the basal ganglia, resulting in compensatory hyperactivity and increased dopamine release. Preclinical, neuroimaging, genetic, and clinical evidence supports that neurodegeneration in PD is preceded by a period of neuronal hyperactivation marked by increased glutamatergic transmission, calcium dysregulation, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction, revealing altered striatal connections and increased dopamine turnover. This hyperdopaminergic disorder manifests clinically as early non-motor symptoms like autonomic dysfunction, REM sleep behavior disorder, and hyposmia. Multimodal biomarkers that combine genetic, imaging, and electrophysiological data can detect this pre-degenerative stage, making early intervention possible. Calcium channel modulators, mitochondrial stabilizers, metabolic regulators, and anti-inflammatory medications that target the NRF2 and PPAR-γ pathways are examples of novel strategies for preserving neuronal integrity. Therefore, redefining PD as a disorder of reversible neuronal stress instead of permanent degeneration can lead to opportunities for both early and long-term neuroprotection.

papers.title: Sub-second Three-dimensional Behavioral Profiling Reveals a Shared Rearing-descent Deficit and Lesion-aligned Lateralization in Parkinsonian Mice.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is expressed through heterogeneous pathological processes, yet preclinical behavioral assays often reduce motor impairment to coarse measures of activity or task performance. Combining AVATAR-based three-dimensional pose tracking with keypoint-MoSeq behavioral segmentation, we longitudinally compared mice with unilateral intrastriatal 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA) lesions and mice with bilateral nigral human A53T α-synuclein overexpression with WT mice and directly with each other. Histology confirmed asymmetric nigrostriatal dopaminergic degeneration in 6-OHDA mice and bilateral midbrain dopaminergic loss with phosphorylated α-synuclein pathology in A53T mice. Although total distance traveled did not differ among the groups, both models showed reduced vertical movement with reduced use and weakened execution of a rearing-associated fast-descent syllable. This deficit did not differ between the models, and the transition from high rearing into this syllable remained reduced at the later timepoint in both models. Within A53T mice, the deficit was associated with residual nigral dopaminergic cell density. 6-OHDA mice showed lesion-aligned lateral-flexion and rotational biases in both syllable usage and within-syllable execution, and most direct differences between the models involved directionally biased syllables. In mice assessed at both timepoints, the lateral bias of 6-OHDA mice decreased within animals, whereas the rearing-descent deficit showed no detectable recovery. These findings identify a rearing-descent deficit shared by two Parkinsonian models that is not captured by global locomotor output, and show that three-dimensional syllable analysis resolves a unilateral lesion into altered syllable usage and biased within-syllable execution.

papers.title: Ubiquitin-Proteasome System: Key Insights into Neurological Disorder Mechanisms.
papers.abstract: The ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) is crucial for maintaining protein homeostasis in the central nervous system. Dysfunction of the UPS leads to the accumulation of neurotoxic aggregates, including amyloid, tau, alpha-synuclein, SOD1, and TDP-43, which are hallmark features of various neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and ALS. Agerelated decline in the UPS and autophagy-lysosomal pathways results in compromised proteostasis and progressive neuronal damage. Current literature from diverse databases provides insights emphasizing the clinical relevance of UPS-targeted interventions. Strategies such as targeted degradation of misfolded proteins, modulation of PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy, and the use of enzyme activators or allosteric modulators show potential in restoring brain homeostasis. This review discusses UPS-mediated proteolytic mechanisms, molecular disruptions associated with disease progression, and emerging therapeutic approaches aimed at enhancing protein clearance.

papers.title: Death-Associated Protein Kinase 1 (DAPK1) Signalling at the Crossroads of Apoptosis, Autophagy, and Post-transcriptional Cascades in Neurodegenerative Diseases.
papers.abstract: Death-associated Protein Kinase-1 is a Ca2+/calmodulin- dependent serine/threonine protein kinase which controls various cellular processes and functions, including apoptosis, autophagy, and post-transcriptional processes, through multiple microRNAs. Increasing evidence suggests that, aberrant increase in the level of DAPK1 may result in neuronal injury and neurodegeneration by integration of multiple pathological processes such as excitotoxicity, neuroinflammation, and protein aggregation. DAPK1 contributes to disease progression through mechanisms such as NMDA receptor-mediated excitotoxicity, tau and α-synuclein hyperphosphorylation, apoptotic signaling, autophagic dysregulation, and synaptic loss. This review overviews the structural organization, regulatory mechanisms and role of DAPK1 in various cellular processes involved in neurodegeneration. This review discusses the complex transcriptional, post-transcriptional, and post-translational mechanisms governing DAPK1 activity, including regulation by transcription factors, microRNAs, phosphorylation events, and protein degradation pathways. Particular highlighting is given to the involvement of DAPK1 in both chronic and acute neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, diabetic encephalopathy, traumatic brain injury, and cerebral ischemic stroke. Finally, current therapeutic approaches based on the modulation of DAPK1 activity, including kinase inhibitors, competitive peptides, and gene-regulatory approaches, are reviewed, along with the challenges associated with target selectivity, blood-brain barrier penetration, and clinical translation. Collectively, this review emphasizes the therapeutic potential and discusses future directions for the development of disease-modifying interventions targeting DAPK1 in neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.title: 27-Hydroxycholesterol Modulates Microglial α-Synuclein Handling and Is Associated with AKT1/JAK-STAT/TNF Signaling in Parkinson's Disease Models.
papers.abstract: 27-Hydroxycholesterol (27-OHC) is an oxysterol implicated in neuroinflammation, but its relationship to microglial α-synuclein (α-syn) handling and intracellular signaling in Parkinson's disease (PD) models remains incompletely defined. We combined BV2-cell assays, an rAAV-A53T mouse model, untargeted lipidomics and proteomics, network analyses, molecular docking, pathway immunoblotting, pharmacological AKT inhibition, and a cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA). In BV2 cells, 0.5-2.5 μM 27-OHC did not reduce viability, whereas concentrations ≥ 5 μM were cytotoxic. At 2.5 μM, 27-OHC increased cell-associated α-syn signal after exposure to recombinant α-syn PFFs. Brain lipidomics in the PD model showed accumulation of the broad sterol-lipid class, but did not provide absolute brain 27-OHC concentrations. Network analyses nominated AKT1, IL6, STAT3, and MMP9 as hub genes. In three independent BV2 experiments, PFF and 27-OHC exposure were associated with altered phosphorylation of AKT, STAT3, and NF-κB p65; a PFF × 27-OHC interaction was detected for STAT3 phosphorylation. MK-2206 lowered the cell-associated α-syn/GAPDH signal in the combined-treatment group, although the comparison did not remain significant after adjustment across three pairwise tests. CETSA showed greater soluble AKT1 retention after 27-OHC exposure and a higher thermal-curve area under the curve (paired p = 0.023). These findings support an association between 27-OHC exposure, microglial α-syn handling, and AKT-related signaling in BV2 cells. They do not establish direct 27-OHC-AKT1 binding or an in vivo causal effect of brain 27-OHC on microglia.

papers.title: Effects of mind-body exercise on motor function, quality of life, and depressive symptoms in patients with Parkinson's disease: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: This study used network meta-analysis to compare and rank the effects of different mind-body exercises on motor function, depression, and quality of life in patients with Parkinson's disease, to inform clinical practice. METHODS: PubMed, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Embase, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Database, and VIP Database were searched from inception to June 8, 2026, for randomized controlled trials of mind-body exercise interventions in Parkinson's disease. Network meta-analysis was performed using Stata version 18.0. Direct and indirect evidence was synthesized, and interventions were ranked using the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA). Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool and the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, respectively. RESULTS: A total of 43 studies involving 2,337 patients with Parkinson's disease were included. For balance measured using the Berg Balance Scale, dance was significantly more effective than no treatment, walking, and usual care. For functional mobility measured using the Timed Up and Go Test, qigong was significantly more effective than tai chi, Dance, stretching, no treatment, and usual care. For overall motor function measured using the Unifed Parkinson's Disease rating Scale, Part III, yoga was significantly more effective than usual care and no treatment. For depressive symptoms measured using the Hamilton Depression Scale, tai chi was significantly more effective than qigong, no treatment, walking, and usual care. For health-related quality of life, as measured by the Parkinson's Disease Questionnaire, qigong was significantly more effective than usual care. papers.title: Association of pre-clinical depressive symptoms and its plasma metabolomic signature with Parkinson's disease: a community-based longitudinal study.
papers.abstract: Accumulating evidence has suggested that depression is associated with an increased risk of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet whether pre-clinical depressive symptoms in PD development and the potential mediating effects of metabolomic profiles remain unclear. We aimed to examine the association between depressive symptoms and PD risk, evaluate effect modification by genetic susceptibility, and assess metabolomic mediation. This prospective study included 451,922 PD-free participants from the UK Biobank. Depressive symptoms were collected by a 2-item Patient Health Questionnaire (range, 0-6; ≥3 indicates possible depressive disorder) at baseline. Identification of PD was based on medical records. papers.title: Integrating wavelet signal processing and machine learning for EEG-based detection of brain diseases with representative channel selection.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
papers.abstract: BackgroundBrain diseases pose a significant global health challenge, and their diagnosis often relies on subjective clinical assessments.ObjectiveTo this end, this study proposes an integrated wavelet signal processing and machine learning framework for single-channel Electroencephalography (EEG)-based detection of brain diseases with representative channel selection.MethodsFirst, EEG signals are decomposed into rhythm-specific sub-bands using the Discrete Wavelet Packet Transform (DWPT). Then, for each rhythm, a multi-dimensional feature matrix (MFM) is constructed by integrating Approximate Entropy (AE), Rhythm Energy Ratio (RER), C0-complexity (C0), and Zero-crossing Rate (ZCR), which comprehensively models the EEG characteristics. Six classifiers were compared under subject-level leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, and Decision Tree (DT) was selected as the representative classifier. Each channel was then evaluated independently as a complete single-channel system, and representative channels were identified from the completed results.ResultsValidated on publicly available datasets for SCHIZ (schizophrenia), UNM (Parkinson's disease), and MPHCE (depression), the method achieves impressive accuracies of 84.52% (F4), 86.54% (F4), and 93.10% (Fp1), respectively, using single-channel EEG electrode.ConclusionsSuch results demonstrate that the proposed approach maintains robust detection performance in each of the three disease-specific tasks. The framework is lightweight by design, using only a single EEG channel and a single simple machine-learning model for classification. It needs no multi-channel feature concatenation or decision-level fusion. This single-channel design suits hardware and data sources with limited resources, and may support the development of low-cost portable EEG systems.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of a series of Tianma Gouteng decoctions for Parkinson's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This meta-analysis aimed to systematically assess the efficacy and safety of a series of Tianma Gouteng decoctions (TGDs) as adjunctive therapy for the treatment of Parkinson's disease (PD) using the latest clinical evidence. METHODS: Nine databases were searched from their inception to 31 August 2025 to identify eligible studies. Primary outcomes included the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS), Traditional Chinese Medicine Syndrome Score (TCMSS) and clinical efficacy. Secondary outcomes encompassed the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), British 39-item Parkinson's Disease Questionnaire (PDQ-39), Hamilton Depression Scale (HAMD), Parkinson's Disease Sleep Scale (PDSS), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), malondialdehyde (MDA), superoxide dismutase (SOD) and adverse events. The Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach was used to assess the quality of evidence. RESULTS: Thirty-four randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving a total of 3049 participants were ultimately included. The results indicated that add-on therapy with TGDs significantly benefited patients with PD by reducing the UPDRS, TCMSS, PDQ-39, and HAMD scores, as well as IL-6, TNF-α and MDA levels, and by increasing clinical efficacy, the MMSE, MoCA, and PDSS scores, and SOD levels. TGDs also reduced the incidence of adverse events, including constipation, gastrointestinal reactions, and the on-off phenomenon. CONCLUSIONS: This meta-analysis provided up-to-date and supportive evidence for the efficacy and safety of TGDs as adjunctive therapy in the treatment of patients with PD. Given the generally low certainty of the evidence, more high-quality RCTs are recommended to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Prelimbic cortex CRHR1 regulates Parkinson's disease-related anxiety through a PrLGlu-avBNSTGABA-VTADA pathway.
papers.abstract: Anxiety is a common non-motor symptom of Parkinson's disease (PD). Due to the unclear mechanism, treatment becomes challenging and significantly impacts the quality of life of patients. Although corticotropin-releasing hormone receptor 1 (CRHR1) is abundantly expressed in the prelimbic cortex (PrL) and have been implicated in PD and anxiety, the role and mechanism of PrL CRHR1 in PD-related anxiety remain unclear. By combining neuropharmacological, chemogenetic, neuroanatomical, and molecular approaches, the present study were performed to investigate the role of PrL CRHR1 in PD-related anxiety and to explore its neural pathways. In this study, unilateral 6-hydroxydopamine lesions of the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) in male Sprague-Dawley rats induced anxiety-like behaviors and decreased CRHR1 expression in the PrL compared to sham rats. In sham and the lesioned rats, pharmacological blockade of PrL CRHR1 induced anxiety-like behaviors, whereas its activation produced anxiolytic-like effects, with both effects attenuated in the lesioned rats. CRHR1 blockade was accompanied by increased c-Fos expression in the anterior ventral bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (avBNST), while selective knockdown of CRHR1 in avBNST-projecting PrLGlu

papers.title: A multimodal mobile dataset for Parkinson's disease symptom assessment.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) affects both motor and non-motor functions, often progressing gradually and remaining undiagnosed in its early stages. To support research aimed at earlier and more accessible detection, we introduce UT-MoDaPark, a multimodal dataset collected through a mobile application designed to capture a broad spectrum of PD-related symptoms. The dataset includes recordings from 151 participants (68 individuals with clinically confirmed PD and 83 healthy controls) collected in structured, in-person sessions to ensure consistency and reliability. Participants engaged in five interactive modules using a tablet: a drawing task for assessing fine motor control, a selfie-based facial expression task, a voice-based emotion recognition task, a structured symptom questionnaire, and a gamified voice control exercise. The released dataset includes drawing trajectories, facial landmarks and Action Units, voice-derived features, questionnaire responses, and participant metadata. UT-MoDaPark offers a unified and symptom-rich resource that can support the development of digital tools for early detection, remote monitoring, and personalized assessment of PD, with particular relevance to real-world, at-home, or low-resource healthcare settings.

papers.title: Continuous Recording of Local Field Potentials via Deep Brain Stimulation Electrodes in Parkinson's Disease:A Technical and Conceptual Review.
papers.journal: The journal of medical investigation : JMI
papers.abstract: Recent advances in deep brain stimulation (DBS) devices equipped with sensing capabilities have enabled continuous recording of local field potentials (LFPs) in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD). This review provides an overview of current knowledge on diurnal variations in LFPs in PD and summarizes the technical features of the representative sensing-enabled DBS system, Percept™ PC/RC. Previous studies have reported fluctuations in beta-band activity across the day, suggesting associations with dopaminergic and behavioral rhythms. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating diurnal variations for understanding PD pathophysiology and optimizing adaptive DBS (aDBS) strategies. The Percept™ PC/RC allows continuous LFP recording, facilitating studies of long-term neural activity in naturalistic settings. Future directions include the development of individualized stimulation strategies based on continuous and multimodal symptom tracking. By integrating conceptual and methodological perspectives, this review aims to guide future research toward more precise and personalized neuromodulation in PD. J. Med. Invest. 73 : 295-301, August, 2026.

papers.title: Task-state prefrontal cortex activation differences between executive dysfunction and perceptual dysfunction phenotypes of freezing of gait in Parkinson's disease during the medication ON state: a retrospective fNIRS study.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The dual-model pathophysiological framework of freezing of gait (FOG) in Parkinson's disease proposes that, in some patients, freezing arises predominantly from impaired frontostriatal executive control (the executive dysfunction model), whereas in others it arises predominantly from impaired posterior-cortical visuospatial/perceptual processing (the perceptual dysfunction model). This framework therefore predicts opposite, task-specific patterns of impaired cortical activation in the two patient groups during executive and visuospatial tasks. OBJECTIVE: To compare prefrontal cortical (PFC) activation during seated cognitive tasks in the medication ON state between two proposed FOG phenotypes in Parkinson's disease (PD): PD-FOG-EDF, based on the executive dysfunction model, and PD-FOG-PDF, based on the perceptual dysfunction model, thereby testing these predictions. METHODS: This retrospective study included 125 participants: PD-FOG-EDF (n = 32), PD-FOG-PDF (n = 28), PD without FOG (PD-nFOG, n = 35), and healthy controls (n = 30). Participants underwent neuropsychological testing, wearable gait analysis, and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) during a verbal fluency task (VFT) and Benton Line Orientation Test (BLOT). Assessments were performed in the ON state 60-120 min after dopaminergic medication; freezing episodes were objectively recorded by synchronized video and inertial sensors. Analyses included covariate-adjusted models, Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction, and internal validation by bootstrap, leave-one-out, and repeated 5-fold cross-validation. RESULTS: PD-nFOG showed a lower MoCA score than HC but a higher score than both FOG groups, mildly reduced VFT, TMT, and SCWT performance relative to HC, and BLOT performance comparable to HC, without selective impairment of any single cognitive domain. papers.title: A COSMIN systematic review of performance-based assessment tools for mealtime performance in Parkinson's disease: a linking study based on the ICF framework.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: This study systematically reviewed performance-based outcome measurement instruments (PerFOMs) for mealtime performance in Parkinson's disease and appraised their measurement domains and properties using the ICF framework and COSMIN methodology. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, ProQuest, and CINAHL were searched for studies published between January 2006 and July 2026. Eligible studies used observer-administered PerFOMs that evaluated comprehensive ingestive skills during meals. Patient-reported outcome measures and screening tools limited to isolated swallowing tasks were excluded. Instrument items were linked to ICF components, and measurement properties were appraised using COSMIN. RESULTS: Two studies were included, identifying two PerFOMs: the Mealtime Assessment Scale (MAS) and the modified Older Americans Resources and Services (OARS) scale. The MAS was linked to all four ICF components, whereas the modified OARS scale was limited to utensil use. Neither instrument had undergone independent content-validity testing. The MAS showed adequate methodological quality with sufficient results for measurement error and convergent validity, whereas the modified OARS scale lacked evidence for most measurement properties. CONCLUSIONS: The evidence base for comprehensive mealtime assessment in PD remains limited and preliminary. Existing instruments differ in ICF coverage and lack content validation. Further research should establish psychometric evidence and address multiple dimensions of mealtime performance in PD.

papers.title: Flexible recording electrodes preliminarily reveal the brain-spinal circuit mechanism of spinal cord stimulation in the treatment of motor impairment in the mouse model of Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by motor impairment, including gait disorders and postural instability, while the efficacy of pharmacological therapy and deep brain stimulation remains limited. In recent years, the potential of spinal cord electrical stimulation (SCS) has attracted significant attention in the treatment of movement disorders, but its underlying mechanism remains unclear. Owing to their excellent biocompatibility and high spatiotemporal resolution, flexible recording electrodes are regarded as important tools for decoding the motor circuits. In the present study, flexible recording electrodes were used to chronically record brain signals in the PD mouse model and to explore the regulatory mechanism of SCS in the brain-spinal cord motor circuit. The results demonstrate that SCS effectively ameliorates motor impairment in the PD mouse model. Moreover, the spectral power of the theta-band (4-10 Hz) recorded in the primary motor (M1) cortex of PD mice significantly increased after SCS. Collectively, this study comprehensively evaluated the therapeutic effects of SCS in a PD mouse model and identified cortical theta-band activity as a potential electrophysiological marker, which may provide evidence for the closed-loop application of SCS in clinical practice.

papers.title: Environmental influences on visual hallucinations in Lewy body disease: the potential role of virtual reality.
papers.abstract: Lewy body disease (LBD), which includes Parkinson's disease (PD) and dementia with Lewy bodies, is frequently accompanied by visual hallucinations, one of its most characteristic neuropsychiatric symptoms. These symptoms are clinically significant as they reduce quality of life, increase caregiver burden, and correlate with poorer prognosis. In clinical practice, visual hallucinations in LBD often appear under certain environmental conditions, including nighttime or low light settings, ambiguous shadows or patterns, and visual features such as furniture or decorations, suggesting environmental influence. However, this dependency has not been systematically characterized, and its mechanisms remain partially understood. Current evidence suggests that this phenomenon may arise from the interaction of reduced bottom-up visual input, excessive top-down influence, and impaired reality monitoring. Although pharmacological treatments remain crucial, adverse events and tolerability concerns often limit their use and increase discontinuation rates. Thus, investigating non-pharmacological approaches such as direct modifications to patients' environment may provide an alternative approach to symptom management and treatment. In this Perspective article, we summarize the clinical features of visual hallucinations in LBD, review evidence regarding their environmental dependency, examine candidate pathophysiological mechanisms, and highlight virtual reality as a promising tool for mechanistic investigation and individualized environmental interventions.

papers.title: Gut-brain-muscle axis in patients with Parkinson's disease.
papers.journal: The journal of medical investigation : JMI
papers.abstract: Patients with Parkinson's disease (PD), their caregivers, and clinicians encounter a range of motor and non-motor symptoms. The motor symptoms can affect the extremities, trunk, orofacial region, and pharyngolaryngeal structures, whereas the non-motor symptoms include such features as cognitive decline, psychiatric symptoms, sleep disturbance, autonomic nervous dysregulation, and gastrointestinal symptoms. The diversity and interplay of these symptoms make PD one of the most challenging neurodegenerative diseases to manage. Because multiple symptom domains are simultaneously vulnerable in PD-resembling the multidimensional frailty observed in older adults-maintaining patients' adaptability to daily living is a central therapeutic goal. In this context, we employ the concept of the "gut-brain-muscle axis" as a framework for supporting resilience and mitigating the progression of frailty. This concept emphasizes the bidirectional communication between the gastrointestinal system with its microbiota, the central nervous system, and the musculoskeletal system, and highlights how dysfunction in one component can propagate to others, thereby accelerating the progression of frailty. Here, we introduce this concept and discuss how it can be adapted to prevent frailty in PD patients. J. Med. Invest. 73 : 310-318, August, 2026.
